jess (sales): Hey team — running a demo for Acme corp and their trial key is getting 403s on /v1/generate. Customer on the call, need quick triage.

maria (sales-eng): Thanks for the heads up. Any logs or exact error? 403 usually authz or org binding.

jess (sales): Error payload: "error: access_denied (key bound to different org)". Customer says they set X-Org-Id header to their tenant id.

alex (eng): Can you paste the exact curl they used? sometimes the header name or casing is wrong. Also which endpoint — hosted or dedicated?

jess (sales): Hosted. Their curl:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer SK_ABC123" -H "X-Org-Id: org-998" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

maria (sales-eng): Two quick checks: 1) confirm SK_ABC123 is the key we issued to org-123 (not org-998). 2) check if they're including an extra Project header (X-Project-Id) that might be scoped to a different org.

miguel (devops): I pulled the key binding from auth logs: SK_ABC123 -> org-123, no project bound. When a request has X-Org-Id that doesn't match key binding, we return 403.

john (customer): We definitely used the tenant id from our dashboard. Could that be stale?

alex (eng): Possible. The tenant id in onboarding can differ from account id if we created a short-lived demo tenant. Could you run this on your side to confirm header and response?
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer SK_ABC123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/account/keys
```

john (customer): running...

sre-bot: deploy detected: auth-service v2.14.3 deployed 2024-04-14T18:07:12Z — no incidents reported.

john (customer): Response shows key bound to org-123. Looks like dashboard shows org-998 — weird.

maria (sales-eng): OK that explains it. They have two orgs; the key is for org-123 but they used org-998 in the header. Options: 1) remove X-Org-Id header so key binding is used by default, or 2) reissue a key bound to org-998. Which is preferable?

john (customer): For the demo we can remove the header. How do we remove it in their SDK?

alex (eng): In the JS SDK, don't pass the org option. Example:
```js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
const res = await client.generate({ prompt: 'hi' });
```
If they need to target a different org, we need to issue a key for that org.

john (customer): Removed header, now 200. Thanks!! :tada:

jess (sales): Huge win for the demo. John — quick Q: asking about per-call pricing tiers while you're on the call. Can I loop in pricing-bot for starter estimate?

pricing-bot: Based on your sample usage (2k tokens/minute for demo) estimated hosted cost ~$0.40/min. See https://redwood.ai/pricing.

john (customer): Great, will evaluate. Also need to finish security questionnaire for procurement — is there a contact?

maria (sales-eng): I can own the security Qs. @john can you DM me the vendor form or upload to the portal? We'll assign SOC2 artifact links and a dedicated CSM.

jess (sales): Follow-up action items: 1) reissue key for org-998 if they want explicit binding (maria to confirm), 2) send pricing summary and contract options (jess), 3) security questionnaire handoff (maria).

maria (sales-eng): I'll open a ticket and attach the SOC2 and data-handling docs. Also note: if they later use Dedicated, key binding rules differ (we can set org-level tokens).

alex (eng): For internal note: auth logs show 3 failed attempts from the demo IP before success. No rate-limit hits.

miguel (devops): If they request rotation, we can create a short-lived demo key scoped to their demo project — let me know.

john (customer): Thanks everyone, demo recovered. I'll DM the security doc.

jess (sales): Great job team :thumbsup:

maria (sales-eng): Closing this thread. Will follow up in the ticket with artifacts and the key reissue if requested.
